title: Committed throughput SLO banding and notice-to-remediate process
creator: Avery Chen
description: Define formal SLO/SLA definitions, error-budget accounting, and contract language for committed throughput on Dedicated fleets. The doc must reconcile short-window detection for fast remediation with long-window credits for customer fairness, and specify how autoscaling events affect measurement and credit computation.
acceptance_criteria: Written SLA clause example suitable for inclusion in commercial contract annex (plain English + legal-friendly table)
Definition of measurement methodology (metrics, aggregation window, percentile) agreed with runtime and instrumentation teams
Error budget model documented: how credits accrue/expire, how they are consumed by incidents and autoscale events
Playbook for notice-to-remediate and credit issuance with roles, SLAs for Redwood response, and escalation path
notes: Context: Customers buying Dedicated capacity expect predictable sustained throughput for their reserved GPUs. Current proposals in other tickets focus on credit formulas but do not handle rolling autoscale events or transient network blips.

We must avoid over-compensating for short-lived tail latency while also ensuring customers can claim credits for sustained degradation. Proposed approach uses dual-window detection + proportional crediting.
Related internal artifacts: PRD draft, observability dashboard queries, prototype credit calculator (spreadsheet)

decisions: Use dual-window measurement: 5-minute detection window for rapid detection (used for alerts and runbook activation) and 1-hour rolling window for credit eligibility and error-budget accounting.

Primary metric: per-customer served throughput (tokens/minute) normalized to committed capacity. SLO evaluated as 95th percentile of 1-hour rolling windows over a 30-day period for contract compliance reporting.

Error budget buckets: 'transient' (<5 minutes) are logged and reviewed but do not automatically generate credits; 'sustained' (>15 minutes within 1-hour window) consume error budget and may generate credits.

Autoscale events: capacity increases triggered by Redwood autoscaler will pause credit accrual for the duration of the autoscale event plus 10 minutes, provided autoscale eliminated the capacity shortfall. Customer-requested manual scale downs are excluded from credit eligibility.

Credit computation: proportional entitlement = max(0, 1 - observed_throughput / committed_throughput) averaged across the 1-hour window, applied to customer's monthly invoice as percent credit capped at 30% per incident and 60% aggregate per month.

Measurement exclusions: scheduled maintenance windows (pre-notified) and customer-side misconfiguration demonstrated by request logs are excluded from credits. All exclusions must be recorded in the incident timeline in the SRE portal.
contract_language_examples: Example clause (plain language): 'Redwood guarantees that Dedicated capacity will provide committed throughput as measured by the 95th percentile of per-customer served throughput over rolling one-hour windows. If Redwood fails to meet committed throughput for a sustained event (defined as >15 minutes of observed shortfall within a one-hour window), customer will be eligible for service credits as described below.'

Example clause (legal appendix): 'Service Credit = min(0.30, 1 - (ObservedHourlyThroughput / CommittedHourlyThroughput)). Service Credits will be applied to the invoice for the month in which the Event occurred. Aggregate Service Credits in any calendar month shall not exceed 0.60 of that month’s Dedicated Capacity fees.'

Notice and remediation: 'Customer must provide Redwood written notice of a claimed SLA breach within 30 days of occurrence. Redwood shall investigate and respond within 5 business days with preliminary findings and expected remediation timeline.'
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (Instrumentation): ENG to add per-customer throughput metrics, autoscale event tagging, and metric export (ENG-48122). Target: 2025-02-14.
Phase 2 (Detection & Dashboard): Observability to implement 5m and 1h rolling queries + incident dashboard. Link to dashboard proto: https://dashboard.internal.redwood/platform/dedicated/slo-proto

Phase 3 (Credit Engine): Implement credit calculator service (stateless function that consumes metrics and incident timeline) and integration with billing. Shipping in beta tied to release dedicated-2025.03.
Phase 4 (Legal & GTM): Finalize contract language and go/no-go for including new SLA in sales materials and self-serve UI. Legal review required before public rollout.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Per-customer throughput measurement may be noisy for bursty workloads. Mitigation: use percentile-based aggregation and minimum-observation thresholds (e.g., ignore windows with <5% of expected baseline traffic).

Risk: Autoscale interplay could cause disputes if scaling is delayed. Mitigation: tag autoscale events and include them in incident timelines, pause crediting during corrective autoscale periods, and surface the autoscale schedule to sales/legal.
Risk: Credit caps may not satisfy large enterprise customers. Mitigation: offer addendum options for higher credit caps under dedicated enterprise contracts (sales to route to Legal).
